pr_title: Moved OPENSSL_fork_prepare,_parent,_child from init.c to threads_pthread.c
pr_body:
These methods have been deprecated. The move is to insulate non-UNIX platforms from these undefined symbols.

CLA: Permission is granted by the author to the OpenSSL team to use these modifications.

Fixes #13273

Signed-off-by: Randall S. Becker <rsbecker@nexbridge.com>
pr_comments: Is there an "OpenSSL" way of marking methods as being potentially subject to deprecation? I'm thinking that these three need that.

> being potentially subject to deprecation? 

We have a way of marking them as deprecated. See internal/man7/deprecation.pod and/or #13240 that updates that documentation.
@mattcaswell I pushed a new commit 60adea7932 to attempt to mark these as deprecated. If I got it correct, then we can add it to this PR. Otherwise, we can ignore it.
Oh...and you'll need to run `make update` once you've made the above changes.

> 
> 
> Please could you also add an entry to CHANGES.md saying that these functions are deprecated, and that there is no need to call anything instead.

It's in the commit 13efbe0. Hopefully I got the language correct.
I think AppVeyor is having issues.
So defining deprecated methods breaks Travis. I think I'm going to need some help here.
@mattcaswell I'm having problems with deprecation and the default builds. Both Travis and AppVeyor are failing on me based on requested changes. Can you assist?
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged with small amendment (stray whitespace on end of line in OPENSSL_fork_prepare.pod removed). Thank you for the PR.

issue_context.title: Missing fork methods in PUT builds on NonStop
issue_context.body:
In 3.0, the following methods are missing from the POSIX user thread build, referenced by `liblegacy-lib-threads_pthread.o`:

* `OPENSSL_fork_prepare`
* `OPENSSL_fork_child`
* `OPENSSL_fork_parent`

This occurs during the link phase of `providers\legacy.so`.
comments:
This appears to occur because of:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/648cf9249e6ec60e0af50d5d903e05244b837cb0/crypto/init.c#L669

not being defined for NonStop platforms. The following might solve this:

```
#if defined OPENSSL_SYS_UNIX || defined OPENSSL_SYS_TANDEM
```
If appropriate, I will create a PR for this.

Hmm. They are defined in init.c - and that file is not included when building liblegacy:

````
$UTIL_COMMON=\
        cryptlib.c params.c params_from_text.c bsearch.c ex_data.c o_str.c \
        ctype.c threads_pthread.c threads_win.c threads_none.c initthread.c \
        context.c sparse_array.c asn1_dsa.c packet.c param_build.c $CPUIDASM \
        param_build_set.c der_writer.c passphrase.c
$UTIL_DEFINE=$CPUIDDEF

SOURCE[../libcrypto]=$UTIL_COMMON \
        mem.c mem_sec.c \
        cversion.c info.c cpt_err.c ebcdic.c uid.c o_time.c o_dir.c \
        o_fopen.c getenv.c o_init.c init.c trace.c provider.c \
        punycode.c \
        $UPLINKSRC
SOURCE[../providers/libfips.a]=$UTIL_COMMON
SOURCE[../providers/liblegacy.a]=$UTIL_COMMON
````
I have no idea why they are included in init.c. The only place they are ever referenced from internally is threads_pthread.c - and they are only relevant in a pthreads build. I'd suggest we move their definitions (which are empty anyway) in threads_pthread.c.

The alternative is to remove them completely. They are totally unused, and do nothing - but they do form part of the public API.

My impression from the documentation is that external developers can fill these in with whatever they need on a platform basis. Doesn't help though. It has me scratching my head as to why these are being referenced  through that guard, but they are.

> My impression from the documentation is that external developers can fill these in with whatever they need on a platform basis.

No. The idea is that applications can call these manually to inform OpenSSL about forks - if OpenSSL is running on a platform where it can't detect the fork itself. I think the original idea was that OpenSSL would do something in response to this information (e.g. reseed the DRBG). However in practice calls to these functions are ignored and have been ever since they were first introduced in 1.1.1. So they are no-ops and always have been no-ops. I doubt very much anyone is actually calling them, so we probably could just delete them entirely and no-one would notice. However strictly speaking that is an API break that would require an OMC vote.
@mattcaswell 's summary is correct and they should at least be deprecated.
I'm just testing the change to move the content from init.c to threads_pthread.c, which should ensure that the build works without changing functionality and will push when it's done.
Aside: I'm finding other configuration nits around PUT and SPT builds. Will open those as a separate issue. Very small cleanup changes in 50-nonstop.conf. :(

> However in practice calls to these functions are ignored and have been ever since they were first introduced in 1.1.1

Technically they were used for a while for actual robust DRBG fork-safety, which got ripped out in favor of the simple pid-based mechanism by https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/9832 (so the use never made it into a release).
@kaduk well the PR should be ready in any event.

review_comments: We should wrap these implementations in `#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0`
You still need to wrap the *implementations* in `#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0` - not just the header declarations.
The `pthread_atfork` code will also have to have `#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0` around it so that `fork_once_func` does nothing in the event of a `no-deprecated` build.
